description: Clock divider giving eight divisions of one clock at the same time, with the set of divisions picked by a switch and each output carrying either a gate or a trigger

params.text: Counts upward from the reset with every output starting low, or downward with every output going high on the first clock after the reset
Picks what the division outputs carry: a gate at 10V held for the length of the division, or a 1ms trigger each time that division turns on
Chooses the set of divisions: B1 and B2 give 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256, D gives 2 to 9, and P gives the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19

inputs.text: The clock being divided; the count advances on each rising edge, which needs to pass 2V
A rising edge past 2V clears the count and puts every division output back to its starting state

outputs.text: Divides by 2 in all four modes
Divides by 4 in either binary mode, by 3 in decimal and by 3 in prime
Divides by 8 in either binary mode, by 4 in decimal and by 5 in prime
Divides by 16 in either binary mode, by 5 in decimal and by 7 in prime
Divides by 32 in either binary mode, by 6 in decimal and by 11 in prime
Divides by 64 in either binary mode, by 7 in decimal and by 13 in prime
Divides by 128 in either binary mode, by 8 in decimal and by 17 in prime
Divides by 256 in either binary mode, by 9 in decimal and by 19 in prime

notes: in B1 each output follows the matching bit of a ripple counter; in the other modes an output goes high on every Nth clock and low again on the next one

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
